references.text: The introduction to the Feast of Tabernacles, which lasts seven days, as verse 42 elaborates with the command to dwell in booths
Explains the purpose of dwelling in booths: to remind the children of Israel that God made them live in tents when He brought them out of Egypt
Parallel text about the Feast of Tabernacles, celebrated for seven days in honor of the Lord
The command to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days after the harvest
The Law is to be read aloud to all Israel during the Feast of Tabernacles every seventh year
The people celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles upon their return from exile, as prescribed
The people built booths and lived in them during Nehemiah's time, as written in the Law
Prophetic text stating that all nations will celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles in the end times
Jesus went up to Jerusalem during the Feast of Tabernacles (σκηνοπηγία), the Jewish festival mentioned in Leviticus
On the last great day of the Feast of Tabernacles, Jesus spoke about living water
